title: The emended second-order term of Opera omnia II 31, tested
author: Gerd Graßhoff

witness.note: §27: the MR component as printed in Opera omnia II 31, with note 5

context.title: Euler's geometry of the tide-raising force

true: conclusion: approximately(tMR, 3 * Sf * x * y / (a * a * a * rho) + 3 * Sf * y * (4 * x * x + y * y) / (2 * a * a * a * a * rho)) fails (not of order 2: relative difference 2.0e-02 at ratio 0.01, 2.0e-03 at ratio 0.001, 2.0e-04 at ratio 0.0001)

model.title: Euler's geometry of the tide-raising force

parameters.name: a
parameters.meaning: distance CS of the luminary from the centre of the earth

parameters.name: rho
parameters.meaning: distance CM of the particle from the centre of the earth

parameters.name: Sf
parameters.meaning: absolute force of the luminary: its accelerating force at the distance of one semidiameter of the earth

variables.name: phi
variables.meaning: the angle ACM between the line to the luminary and the line to the particle

objects.name: A
objects.meaning: the point of the sphere through M that has the luminary in its zenith

objects.name: B
objects.meaning: the point that has it in its nadir

objects.name: D
objects.meaning: a point that has it in the horizon

objects.name: E
objects.meaning: the opposite point that has it in the horizon

objects.name: shell
objects.meaning: the sphere about C through the particle

objects.name: P
objects.meaning: foot of the perpendicular from M on CS

observables.name: dir
observables.meaning: direction of the luminary from the centre

observables.name: dist
observables.meaning: SM, the distance of the particle from the luminary

observables.name: fM
observables.meaning: accelerating force on the particle towards S

observables.name: fC
observables.meaning: accelerating force on the centre towards S

observables.name: tMC
observables.defined_by: fM * cos(direction(M, S) - direction(M, C)) - fC * cos(direction(C, S) - direction(M, C))
observables.meaning: the force on the particle less the force on the centre, along MC, towards the centre

observables.name: tMR
observables.defined_by: fM * cos(direction(M, S) - (direction(M, C) + 90°)) - fC * cos(direction(C, S) - (direction(M, C) + 90°))
observables.meaning: the same along MR, normal to MC, towards the side of the luminary

argument.formal: equal(tMR, Sf * a * y / (dist * dist * dist * rho) - Sf * y / (a * a * rho))

by.statement: The proposition is read off the cited constructions: it holds for every parameter value and every state without any hypothesis.

conclusion.notation: tMR ≈ 3·S·x·y / (a³·ρ) + 3·S·y·(4·x² + y²) / (2·a⁴·ρ)   (to second order in ρ / a)
conclusion.formal: approximately(tMR, 3 * Sf * x * y / (a * a * a * rho) + 3 * Sf * y * (4 * x * x + y * y) / (2 * a * a * a * a * rho))

by.statement: The two expressions agree to the stated order in a small ratio: their relative difference falls like that power of the ratio.

conclusion.note: not of order 2: relative difference 2.0e-02 at ratio 0.01, 2.0e-03 at ratio 0.001, 2.0e-04 at ratio 0.0001
